models.name: Model A: Partitioned ALE FSI
models.what_it_computes: Transient leaflet kinematics with coaptation height, diastolic contact pressure map, and peak first principal stress using an anisotropic hyperelastic leaflet model coupled to finite-volume Navier–Stokes on an ALE mesh.

models.name: Model B: Monolithic Stabilized FE FSI
models.what_it_computes: Coupled pressure–velocity–displacement solution for the full cardiac cycle with direct leaflet–leaflet contact, reporting systolic stress fields, coaptation area, and regurgitant orifice area.

models.name: Model C: Immersed Boundary FSI with Reduced-Order Turbulence
models.what_it_computes: Rapid-cycle predictions of opening/closing transients, commissural bending strains, and cycle-to-cycle stress range using shell elements immersed in a lattice-Boltzmann fluid.

mechanisms.name: Diastolic Coaptation Integrity
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Adequate leaflet coaptation area and contact pressure prevent regurgitation and ensure sealing under the diastolic transvalvular pressure gradient.

mechanisms.name: Systolic Leaflet Stress at Peak Flow
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Elevated tensile stress during peak systole is associated with material damage and early structural valve deterioration.

mechanisms.name: Cycle-to-Cycle Stress Range at Commissures
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Stress amplitude during rapid opening/closing drives fatigue, particularly along the commissural free edges.

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored for every model–mechanism pair on a 0–4 Credibility Index (0 none, 1 limited, 2 moderate, 3 strong, 4 compelling), with acceptance defined as ≥3.

spans: For Model A, the partitioned coupling employed subitera-tions at each time step until the interface traction–displacement mismatch fell below 0.5% of the peak diastolic pressure for coaptation assessments and below 0.4% of the peak systolic traction for stress assessments.
